subsystems.name: Preservation and fixation
subsystems.role: stabilises the brain's structure so it can be imaged without decay.

subsystems.name: Imaging
subsystems.role: captures every neuron, axon and synapse at nanometre resolution.
parts: fluorescence and expansion microscopy for molecular labels

subsystems.name: Reconstruction software
subsystems.role: turns terabytes of images into a wiring diagram.
parts: machine-learning segmentation of cells and synapses

subsystems.name: Physiological model
subsystems.role: gives each reconstructed cell realistic firing behaviour.

subsystems.name: Simulation platform
subsystems.role: runs the network fast enough to behave in real time.

subsystems.name: Verification rig
subsystems.role: tests whether the simulation behaves like the original person.

buildSteps.title: Preserve the tissue
buildSteps.detail: Immediately after death, the brain would be chemically fixed by perfusion so proteins and membranes stay in place, then protected against freezing damage and kept cold.

buildSteps.title: Cut and image
buildSteps.detail: The brain would be sliced into tens of thousands of ultrathin sections, each imaged in an electron microscope — a task already done for small animals but never for a whole human brain.

buildSteps.title: Reconstruct the wiring
buildSteps.detail: Software stitches the images into a 3D volume and traces each neuron's branches, labelling the ~10,000 synapses on it. This needs machine learning plus years of human proofreading.

buildSteps.title: Infer cell properties
buildSteps.detail: Every neuron would be assigned a type and a set of electrical and chemical parameters, inferred from physiology experiments and molecular stains, not from the wiring alone.

buildSteps.title: Build the simulation
buildSteps.detail: The wiring graph and cell parameters would be loaded onto a supercomputer that steps the network forward in time, from milliseconds to hours.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate against real brains
buildSteps.detail: The model would be tuned until its activity patterns match recordings from living tissue of the same type.

buildSteps.title: Give it senses and actions
buildSteps.detail: The simulation would be linked to cameras, microphones and robotic or virtual bodies so it can receive input and act.

buildSteps.title: Test and interpret
buildSteps.detail: Behaviour and internal reports would be compared with the original person. Crucially, no test can prove that the simulation is conscious rather than a very good copy — that question is philosophical, not experimental.

prerequisites.why: completed for the 302-neuron worm and mapped in part for fruit flies and mouse cortex; a human brain is roughly a million times larger and is not close.

prerequisites.tech: Scalable electron microscopy and data infrastructure
prerequisites.why: imaging a whole human brain would produce petabytes to exabytes of images needing automated handling.
detailed models of small circuits exist, but whole-brain real-time simulation is far out of reach.

prerequisites.tech: Brain preservation that keeps fine structure
prerequisites.why: aldehyde fixation preserves synapses well for imaging, but whether it preserves the information that makes a person is unproven.

prerequisites.tech: A defensible theory of what must be copied
prerequisites.why: without knowing whether consciousness depends on molecular states, electrical patterns or something else, no scanning plan can be shown to be sufficient.

pathway.milestone: complete connectomes of small animals and partial maps of mammal cortex
pathway.unlocks: automated reconstruction methods and proof that the approach scales at all.

pathway.milestone: a whole mouse brain connectome with cell types and synapse strengths
pathway.unlocks: simulations of a mammalian brain that can be compared with real behaviour.

pathway.milestone: non-destructive or high-fidelity whole-human scanning and preservation
pathway.unlocks: a dataset from which a human emulation could in principle be built.

pathway.milestone: a simulation that passes behavioural tests indistinguishable from the original
pathway.unlocks: intense ethical and legal debate, because a copy's status as the same person would remain unresolved.
only if the consciousness question is answered — this stage is currently speculation, not engineering.
